verdict.summary: Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service and other model-driven apps are reached through the Dataverse Web API with a normal multitenant Microsoft Entra app: there's no Microsoft app review, and the delegated user_impersonation permission inherits each user's Dynamics security roles. The friction is per customer: each environment has its own URL and token audience, an unverified multitenant app gets stepped up to admin consent, and app-only (server-to-server) access requires an admin to create an application user with a custom security role in every environment.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Most of the time goes to getting an environment with Dynamics 365 apps (a trial), since the free Developer Plan environment can't install Dynamics 365 apps.

timeToProd.assumes: A multitenant agent using delegated user_impersonation, made publisher verified so users aren't stepped up to admin consent; if you accept per-customer admin consent, an unverified app works the same day.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program verification for publisher verification (usually 3–5 business days), then each customer's admin consent and, for app-only access, their admin creating an application user.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: There's no Dynamics-specific review. The range reuses the Entra publisher verification path; see the Microsoft guide.

verdict.cost: No developer fee. Your test environment needs Dynamics 365 apps (trial or paid), and each end user who connects needs their own Dynamics 365 license; application users don't consume a paid license.

prerequisites.item: A Microsoft Entra work/school tenant to register the app in
prerequisites.why: Dataverse uses Entra ID as its only OAuth identity provider; personal Microsoft accounts can't sign up.

prerequisites.item: A Dataverse environment with Dynamics 365 apps enabled (for example a Dynamics 365 trial)
prerequisites.why: Dynamics 365 apps can't be installed in a Developer Plan environment, and from 15 Nov 2026 signing up for the Developer Plan no longer creates an environment at all.

prerequisites.item: A second Dataverse tenant for testing multitenant consent
prerequisites.why: Microsoft says testing only in your own tenant isn't a valid test of multitenant behaviour.

prerequisites.item: For app-only access: a managed solution containing a custom security role
prerequisites.why: Application users can't be given the default security roles, and the application user itself can't be shipped in a solution.

scopeTiers.tier: Delegated Dataverse access (acts as the signed-in user)
scopeTiers.impact: Single delegated permission ('Access Dynamics 365 as organization users'); what the agent can read or write is set by the user's Dynamics security roles, not by scopes. Unverified multitenant apps get stepped up to admin consent.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Whether user_impersonation itself is user-consentable was not confirmed in a primary source; the walkthrough tells you to grant admin consent.

scopeTiers.impact: Lets the app list the environments a user can access (ApiUrl, FriendlyName) so the user can pick one. Each environment then needs its own token.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The docs show the resource URL but not the exact scope string; the scope shown follows the Dataverse pattern.

scopeTiers.impact: Tenant admin consent, then an admin creates an application user in each environment and assigns your custom security role. Good for background agents; doesn't consume a license.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: 'Review' here is the customer admin's setup, not a Microsoft review.

steps.title: Get a tenant and a Dynamics 365 environment
steps.detail: Start a Dynamics 365 trial (for example Sales) with a work account so you have an environment with Dynamics 365 apps enabled. Note its URL (https://{org}.crm.dynamics.com).

steps.title: Register a multitenant app in Entra
steps.detail: App registrations > New registration, 'Accounts in any organizational directory'. Add a Web redirect URI and a client secret or certificate.

steps.title: Add the Dynamics CRM delegated permission
steps.detail: API permissions > Add a permission > APIs my organization uses > Dataverse (Dynamics CRM) > Delegated > user_impersonation. Grant admin consent in your own tenant.

steps.title: Implement sign-in, discovery and per-environment tokens
steps.detail: Auth code + PKCE against https://login.microsoftonline.com/organizations. Call GET https://globaldisco.crm.dynamics.com/api/discovery/v2.0/Instances?$select=ApiUrl,FriendlyName, let the user choose, then request {ApiUrl}/user_impersonation and call {ApiUrl}/api/data/v9.2/WhoAmI.

steps.title: Build 429 / Retry-After handling
steps.detail: Service protection limits are per user per web server: 6,000 requests and 20 minutes of execution time per 5-minute window, about 52 concurrent requests. Honour Retry-After and start slow.

steps.title: (App-only) Package a custom security role
steps.detail: Define the minimum table privileges the agent needs in a custom security role, ship it in a managed solution, and script application-user creation for customers (for example with Package Deployer or the Web API).

steps.title: Test in a second tenant
steps.detail: Sign in from a separate trial tenant, accept consent as that tenant's admin, and (for S2S) create the application user there via Power Platform admin center > Environments > S2S > New app user.

steps.title: Get publisher verified
steps.detail: Verify your domain in Entra, enroll and pass Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program verification, then attach the Partner One ID under the app's Branding & properties.

steps.title: Partner Center business verification
steps.detail: Email, identity, employment and business checks on your Partner Center account.

steps.title: Customer admin onboarding
steps.detail: Each customer's admin grants consent (always for S2S), creates the application user and assigns your security role. Delegated users also need a Dynamics license and suitable roles.

agentCanDo: Implement MSAL auth, Global Discovery environment picker and per-environment token cache
Write Dataverse Web API (OData v9.2) queries for accounts, contacts, opportunities and activities
Design a least-privilege custom security role and package it as a managed solution
Script application-user creation and write customer admin setup docs
Build Retry-After / 429 handling for service protection limits
humanMustDo: Start a Dynamics 365 trial or provide a licensed environment
Register the Entra app and grant consent in your tenant
Complete Partner Center verification and publisher verification
Get each customer's admin to consent and create the application user

blockers.symptom: Installing Dynamics 365 apps is only supported on environments that are created with a database with the option to Enable Dynamics 365 apps set to Yes
blockers.cause: You're using a Power Apps Developer Plan environment, which can't install Dynamics 365 apps.
blockers.fix: Use a Dynamics 365 trial or a sandbox environment created with Dynamics 365 apps enabled.

blockers.symptom: AADSTS90094 'needs permission to access resources in your organization that only an admin can grant' for customer users
blockers.cause: Risk-based step-up consent applies to new unverified multitenant apps requesting more than basic sign-in permissions.
blockers.fix: Publisher-verify the app, or send the customer's admin to the admin consent endpoint.

blockers.symptom: Token works for discovery but Dataverse returns 401 for the chosen environment
blockers.cause: Dataverse tokens are audience-specific: you need a token whose scope is that environment's URL.
blockers.fix: Request {ApiUrl}/user_impersonation (or /.default for S2S) per environment and cache tokens by environment.

blockers.symptom: S2S call succeeds in your tenant but fails in a customer's with a user-not-found style error
blockers.cause: No application user bound to your app exists in that customer environment.
blockers.fix: Customer admin creates the application user (Power Platform admin center > Environments > S2S) and assigns your custom role.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Exact error text not documented in the pages we read.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 with 'Number of requests exceeded the limit of 6000 over time window of 300 seconds'
blockers.cause: Service protection limits per user per web server; trial environments have only one web server.
blockers.fix: Honour Retry-After, reduce batch size, and ramp concurrency gradually.

nuances.text: Access tokens last about 60 minutes; refresh tokens follow normal Entra rules (90 days by default for confidential web apps).
Delegated access is only as broad as the user's Dynamics security roles, and impersonated users must be licensed. App-only users avoid a license but need a custom role in each environment.
Besides service protection limits, Power Platform request entitlements (daily request allocations per license) apply separately and accrue even inside batches.
Unmanaged developer environments are deprecated: suspension starts 15 Dec 2026 and deletion 15 Jan 2027, so don't build your test setup on one.
Marketplace (AppSource) listing is optional; Microsoft says multitenant S2S works without listing.
Dynamics 365 Business Central and Finance & Operations use different APIs and endpoints from Dataverse; this guide covers the Dataverse-based apps (Sales, Customer Service, Field Service, Marketing).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Business Central and F&O auth weren't researched.
